name: the founding time
lore:
In the Founding Time, the world pulsated with the raw, untamed heat of the forge. The land was a shifting tapestry; mountains groaned into existence overnight, and forests grew with a predatory hunger, their roots drinking from veins of pure magic. Ecology was a theater of giants—beasts were vast, starlit creatures that knew nothing of fear, only the primal pulse of the earth.

Behavior was dictated by divine proximity. The Firstborn—elf, dwarf, and dragon—moved with a reverent instinct, their lives entwined with the gods who still walked the soil. There was no greed, only the desperate, holy labor of shaping the first civilizations from chaos. Life was a song of survival sung against the backdrop of the Dawn War, where even the smallest sprout possessed a fierce, sentient will to endure. In those days, the world was young, wild, and dangerously alive.
